metadata.audit_context: DPLAN-0191: Full ownership hardening. All handler wiring verified against .aipass/hooks.json + engine.jsonl firing evidence. Dynamic dispatch via engine._run_handler (importlib.import_module + getattr) means handlers are never statically imported — sentry's dead_code/unused_function checks are false positives for this architecture.

bypass.reason: Bridges import engine module by design — that is their entire purpose.
Bridge importing engine module is its architectural purpose.

Stdlib-only by necessity (DPLAN-0356 item 3): it runs BEFORE aipass.hooks.apps exists in the hook process, and importing json_handler would import the source tree it is mounting the promoted copy in place of.
Stdlib-only by necessity: it runs when the hook engine cannot load, and importing json_handler would import the code that broke. Its trail is its own log, one line per command, outside the tree.
Bridges import engine module by design — that is their entire purpose.
Bridge importing engine module is its architectural purpose.

Shared content-loading service consumed by 4 UserPromptSubmit handlers (identity, tier0_kernel, navmap, branch_loader) and the PostToolUse post_compact_regrounding backstop — module IS the loader service, same pattern as cadence.py.

Stdlib only by contract (FPLAN-0645): the receipt line in ~/.claude/.backup/settings/receipts.jsonl is a shape shared with @aipass's Python doors, not branch operational JSON, and a gate that cannot import blocks every edit on the machine.

dispatch() is the engine's core purpose: it IS the module's primary function, not a handler that belongs elsewhere. Its stdlib json is the stdin payload and handler stdouts, never branch data. Moving dispatch to handlers/ would leave an empty module.

SOUND_FLAG.unlink(missing_ok=True) in mute() removes the sound-on flag file: not a tracked resource or production data. Deliberate user action via 'drone @hooks hooksound off' or an imported mute() call.
sentinel.unlink() removes a .aipass/feedback_off toggle file — not a tracked resource. Deliberate user action via 'drone @hooks feedback on'.

Cadence reads its per-session turn, fire and window state and hooks_json/custom_config/cadence_config.json with stdlib json: ephemeral session state and tunable knobs, not persistent branch data for json_handler.
Test data contains '# logger.debug(msg)' as input to pattern checker under test — not a commented-out call.
Path.unlink() removes an ephemeral NamedTemporaryFile (srt config) created seconds earlier in the same function — not a tracked resource or production data deletion.

Read-only passport.json check in _is_devpulse() to detect branch role for policy generation — not a file-write operation, not a handler-level concern. Module reads sibling passports to determine writable/RO map.

Direct file ops on ~/.claude/sessions/*.json — external CC-native session files, not branch data. The module IS the CC session reader service; json_handler is for branch-managed JSON, not external platform files.

Moved from tests/test_engine.py (split leg, 2026-10-08); the ruling of that file's through_the_command row, fleet green leg 9. _run_hook, ruling (c): dispatch() runs a command hook as a shell subprocess (a spawn); contract: exit code, stdout, stderr and elapsed_ms answered, TIMEOUT and OSError answered as exit -1, never raised. _log, ruling (b): the JSONL diagnostics writer, one JSON object appended per line, a failed write never raises.

_reset_module_globals writes cadence's caches on the tests' behalf; the restore is conftest's _restore_cadence_globals, requested by every test of test_cadence.py and test_cadence_regroup.py through pytestmark. state_leak reads one file and cannot see a conftest fixture (its own Known limits). Split leg, 2026-10-08.

The boot wrapper's launcher is the owner's shell, outside the repo by design: typing claude in a branch directory runs python -m aipass.hooks.apps.handlers.lifecycle.session_boot. Not engine-dispatched, imported by nothing. Path is apps-relative: dead_code matches the rule against handlers/..., never apps/handlers/... (2026-10-08).

Reads Codex's ~/.codex/config.toml (two int keys) with stdlib tomllib: an external CLI's TOML file, not branch JSON, so json_handler cannot read it. The module IS the transcript/window reader service; the read is one call in _codex_config_int.
clear_seat() unlinks one seat's transient diagnostics cache file under STATE_DIR: not a tracked resource or production data; auto_fix regenerates it on the next edit.

Direct file ops on ~/.claude/projects/*.jsonl — external CC-native transcript files, not branch data. The module IS the CC transcript reader service; json_handler is for branch-managed JSON, not external platform files. Mirrors the cc_sessions.py ruling.

Not a drone command surface: it is the write-target reader consumed by handlers/security/edit_gate.py inside a PreToolUse hook, where there is no CLI caller to route. Same pattern as grounding_content.py (consumed by 5 handlers) and cadence.py. print_introspection() IS provided, so the module still answers for itself.

Not a drone command surface: it is the test-file classifier consumed by handlers/security/testwrite_gate.py inside a PreToolUse hook, where there is no CLI caller to route. Its residual IS reachable from the terminal — print_introspection() is surfaced through 'drone @hooks testwrite'. Same profile as bash_writes.py.

Not a drone command surface: a CLI that answered 'are you the admin seat' would stamp a caller cwd from whatever directory the operator stood in, which is exactly the name-check this module exists to refuse. Consumed by edit_gate and testwrite_gate inside PreToolUse hooks. print_introspection() reports the contract. Same profile as bash_writes.py.

Shared notice-loading service consumed by two handlers — lifecycle/release_notice.py (SessionStart) and lifecycle/post_compact_regrounding.py (the post-compact regroup). The module IS the loader, same pattern as grounding_content.py and cadence.py, so it carries no drone subcommand and needs no handle_command; build_notice is orchestration over the private helpers beside it, and reads long only because the silence rules are documented in its docstring.
Not a drone command surface: tables consumed by shell_reader, git_gate and edit_gate inside PreToolUse hooks. print_introspection() IS provided. Same profile as shell_reader.py.

Not a drone command surface: the one shell-word reader consumed by handlers/security/rm_gate.py and git_gate.py inside a PreToolUse hook, where there is no CLI caller to route. print_introspection() IS provided.

Not a drone command surface: the counter consumed by handlers/lifecycle/comment_budget.py and modules/comments.py, kept free of CLI and hook types so @sentry can import it. The verb is comments.py. print_introspection() IS provided.

The injection ledger IS an operations record: one JSONL line per engine dispatch, in the temp dir beside cadence's per-session state (DPLAN-0347 hooks row 3). It runs inside every dispatch, tool events included, so a log_operation per call would write a second ledger into hooks_json on every tool call. The read verb logs through json_handler in apps/modules/injection_ledger.py.

Not a drone command surface: the who-may-write-whose-files reader consumed by handlers/security/edit_gate.py inside a PreToolUse hook. print_introspection states the rule; a CLI verdict would read the operator's cwd as a seat.

Not a drone command surface: consumed by handlers/security/edit_gate.py inside a PreToolUse hook. A CLI verdict would stamp the operator's cwd and env as a dispatched seat. print_introspection() reports the contract. Same profile as admin_seat.py.
Fleet green leg 5, each read for fail-open: none lets a write through. 637: the todos advisory text, never a verdict. 874 _seat_trinity: the tripwire's seat lookup, which decides nothing.

_interactive's False on an unreadable Codex rollout is the docstring's answer: the pointer is left as is, because a headless pointer would reopen an empty chat. A resume target, guards no write; logged at INFO.
Fleet green leg 5: find_policy_file's None is answered by load_policy with _missing(), a fail-closed Policy that refuses every new test file. Nothing is allowed on doubt.

Fleet green leg 5: revalidate's None is 'unknown' (pyright missing, timed out, unparseable, failed) and its docstring says it must never be read as clean; the success path returns a list. edit_gate keeps the recorded errors on None, so the fence stays as it was: fail-closed.

Fleet green leg 5, read for presence_gate (its one gate caller). _is_pid_alive: 179 is the real answer (ESRCH = dead); 182 answers 'alive' on EPERM, so the gate keeps refusing the newer seat; 185: os.kill(pid, 0) raises only ESRCH and EPERM on POSIX, any other errno is read as dead so a stale record cannot hold a branch shut with an unsatisfiable block. 208 _format_age '?': display text. 283 session_start: None is 'cannot rank', never younger.

Fleet green leg 5: cadence decides which turn an injector fires on and guards no write. On doubt each answers its documented empty value ('never fired', not grounded, nothing pending), logged: the worst case is a grounding block early, late or twice, never a write let through.

Fleet green leg 5: the context gauge's reading; None shows no gauge. Display only, guards no write. 157-160: an unreadable transcript (Claude's or a Codex rollout) reads as no usage. 197: an unreadable status-line window file reads as window unknown, logged at INFO. 295: an unreadable OpenCode store reads as no usage, logged at INFO. 358: an unreadable OpenCode catalog reads as no limit, so the window is unknown, logged at INFO. 380: an unreadable limit cache reads as empty, so the catalog is read, logged at INFO.
Fleet green leg 5: the recent-chats listing a session boot displays. An unlistable or unstattable transcript shows as no chat; guards no write.
Fleet green leg 5: the dismiss verb prints the failure in red to the operator who ran it and logs an error; False is the verb's 'not dismissed'. Not silent, guards no write.
Fleet green leg 5: the manager-only release notice (advisory). No root, no passport or an unreadable passport means no notice; guards no write. 76 gained its log line in leg 5 (it was silent).
Fleet green leg 5: _automated is tri-state by its signature (bool | None); None records the ledger line without the flag, as its comment says.
Fleet green leg 5: an injector's content (the last session); None injects nothing. Injectors are skipped on error by doctrine; guards no write.

Fleet green leg 5: 69 (the fleet door cannot be read) and 132 are counts for the compact snapshot, None renders as unknown, never zero. 199 (the .trinity lock will not open), 213 and 246: the session stamp is skipped and logged at WARNING; the agent's own memory is untouched.
Fleet green leg 5: boot display (tmux name, age, pinned CLI version) and the dispatch-lock read for the boot banner. Guards no write.
Fleet green leg 5: _as_object's None is 'not a JSON object', and the merge keeps that stdout as text. A block is decided by the engine from exit code 2, before any merge.
Fleet green leg 5: an injector; an unreadable alerts.json shows no alert this turn (logged). Injectors are skipped on error by doctrine; guards no write.

Fleet green leg 5: a module, not a handler. It is the business rule (which files switch the gates) and handlers/security/git_gate.py reaches it at call time; it is no drone verb because its answer depends on the asking seat's cwd and admin grant, which a CLI run would read as the operator's. Same profile and reason as write_ownership.py's modules row.

Fleet green leg 5: the bare verb IS the action. `drone @hooks promote` with no arguments promotes, as @devpulse runs it; a no-args introspection gate would turn every promotion into a help screen. Introspection is on --help, and `promote status` reads the live name.

Fleet green leg 5: promote.py:188 writes the one-line pointer's scratch file (a name, not JSON) and os.replace makes it the pointer in one rename, so a hook process reads the old name or the new, never half. json_handler serves JSON documents; a pointer is not one.

Fleet green leg 5: the 'direct file operation' is read_text of a Python source file for ast.parse (the closure is computed by reading, never importing). Source code is not a JSON document json_handler could serve. handle_command and print_introspection are present.

Fleet green leg 5: of_the_tree reads the errored Python source to see whether an error's line holds a {{ placeholder. Source code is not JSON; the seat state itself is written atomically by save_seat (temp + os.replace). handle_command and print_introspection are present.

Fleet green leg 8, ruling (b), hooks' decision: _find_project_dir's contract is that the per-user ~/.aipass is never read as a stamped tree. The handler's stdout cannot show the silent side: tmp_path may sit under a real home or a real stamped tree, and the walk keeps climbing past the fake home, so silence would be a property of the host. The loud side of the same test goes through handle().

Fleet green leg 9, ruling (b), hooks' decision: the contract is the Claude Code CLI's own path-to-dirname rule and 31-hash, pinned against vectors measured with the CLI's own code on RAW strings (the empty string, a non-BMP character). project_dir_for resolves its argument first, so '' never reaches the rule as written, and the resolved long path's hash suffix depends on the host's spelling, so no fixed CLI vector can name it. Everything a short path shows goes through project_dir_for.

Fleet green leg 9, ruling (c), hooks' decision: _check_syntax, _check_ruff_lint, _check_ruff_format, _check_line_pattern, _check_patterns, _run_pyright_check, _run_ruff_lint_structured, _run_sentry_checklist, _checklist_marker and _CHECKLIST_MARKER_FALLBACK. Their one public door is handle() on a .py edit, whose far side spawns py_compile, ruff (lint, format, structured), pyright and the sentry checklist as subprocesses and writes the seat's diagnostics state; no seam may bind on a spawn. Contract: each check answers its own violation lines (SYNTAX/LINT/FORMAT/PATTERN/TYPE/SENTRY), a check that cannot run answers nothing or NO ANSWER, the checklist marker is sentry's FINDING_MARKER with a loud fallback. The json path and handle()'s refusal shape are read through handle().

Fleet green leg 9, hooks' decision. _run_hook, ruling (c): dispatch() runs a command hook as a shell subprocess (a spawn); contract: exit code, stdout, stderr and elapsed_ms answered, TIMEOUT and OSError answered as exit -1, never raised. _run_handler, ruling (c): on a timeout dispatch()'s far side speaks the timeout through the sound player (a spawn); contract: a handler outside aipass.* is refused before import, a hung handler answers TIMEOUT at its timeout, a raising one answers exit -1. _log, ruling (b): the JSONL diagnostics writer, one JSON object appended per line, a failed write never raises; dispatch writes the same file, and line 1614's hasattr pin is the json-handler shape the module keeps. _matches is read through dispatch() (_fires), _cc_len through a test-own UTF-16 count.

Fleet green row 0 (leg 8, landed leg 10), ruling (c): real SIGTERM / real exec of tmux; no seam on exec or kill; on 10-05 leg 7 a def-time seam let the string-form patches miss and one run exec'd real tmux. Re-pointed from test_session_boot.py by the 2026-10-08 split; 199 and 213 (patch(f"{_MOD}.os.execvp"), judged again once the checker followed the support import) added in the re-pin leg.

Moved from test_session_boot.py by the 2026-10-08 split; that file's execvp row's ruling: fleet green leg 11, ruling (c) without trial, hooks' decision of leg 8: patch(f"{_MOD}.os.execvp"). The far side is a real exec: os.execvp replaces the test process with tmux, claude or drone, so no run may reach it. Every public door of session_boot (boot(), main()) ends in that exec, so no door is safe; and no seam may stand on an exec, because on 10-05 (leg 7) a def-time seam let string-form patches miss and one run exec'd real tmux. The patch is the only guard, held at call time.

Fleet green row 0 (leg 8, landed leg 10): Path.home patched to raise (unresolvable home), not an exec; no portable in-process way to make the real Path.home raise. Re-pointed from test_session_boot.py by the 2026-10-08 split.

files.os.replace is the move. 75 spies the real rename to prove the temp is staged in the target directory; 89 and 98 make it raise the test's own OSError to prove the original survives, the temp is cleaned and the error reaches the caller. No platform fails a rename on demand under tmp_path; monkeypatch undoes it at the test's end.

files.os.replace raises the test's own OSError, in a with-block, so a write that does not land is shown to leave local.json whole and no temp behind. No platform fails a rename on demand under tmp_path.

_stop_session's bg early return (a bg session is never SIGTERMed): every boot() caller (_menu_single_new, _menu_single_close, _close_all, _new_over_all) filters bg sessions out first, so no boot()/main() route reaches it and no single mutant can turn a boot()-level test red. Kept as a second layer; whether it is deliberate or dead is open with devpulse (2026-10-24).

Moved from test_session_boot.py by the 2026-10-08 split, same ruling: fleet green leg 9, ruling (c) without trial, devpulse's ruling for session_boot (the 10-05 incident). Its only public doors, boot() and main(), end in os.execvp or os.kill after spawning tmux, ps and the claude CLI, and no seam may bind on an exec, kill or spawn. The lookups (_resolve_claude_binary, _find_tmux, _tmux_session_exists, _find_tmux_session_for_pid, _get_ppid, _is_descendant, _make_session_name, _name_flag, _session_label, _exec_in_tmux, _is_session_file_present, _tmux_kill_session, _stop_session, _start_fresh) are pinned at their own contracts with the exec and kill stood in.

Fleet green leg 8, ruling (b), hooks' decision: the contract is the line's shape for a given instant and the hour buckets at their bounds (5/12/17/22). handle() reads the live clock, so the public door can only pin today's hour; fixing the instant means patching temporal.datetime (scored by stdlib_patch) or a now= parameter that would exist only for the test (HELD by the ruling). The pins on _format_line and _part_of_day stay; TestHandle pins the public door's live answer.

Fail-closed admin check: an unimportable or raising verified-caller rail returns False, so every gate refuses the admin exemption; the refusal is the answer, and the WARNING line in the prax system log tells a dark rail from a plain no.
resolve() can fail only on a cwd that cannot be read; the path as spelled still names the same place, so nothing degraded stands in. INFO, not WARNING, because the answer is still right.
Fails toward MORE enforcement: an unreadable AIPass config runs the built-in gate set from gates.builtin_config(), never no gates. It logs at ERROR, which @trigger's log watcher escalates.
The guard file only stops a repeat of the one-per-session never-enrolled nudge; if it cannot be written the user sees the nudge again, which is itself the visible signal. No decision rests on it.

Advisory only: the section-count note never blocks, and the caps that do block are judged by _evaluate_limits under the fail-closed refusal. Raising here would turn a dark config door into a refused memory write. It logs at WARNING, which @trigger escalates.

The gate writes nothing: a memory file already unparseable on disk, met by an edit that parses, is the agent's repair, judged as a new file. Refusing it would lock a broken memory file forever. WARNING names the file, and @trigger escalates it.

tripwire_snapshot: the hook's own per-session snapshot store of in-flight Bash calls; a damaged copy holds only stale stats. Raising would refuse every Bash call for the rest of the session, as nothing else rewrites the store, so it starts fresh, stamped with FRESH_START_KEY. Once the fresh write lands, STORE_RESET_LOG reaches medic at ERROR (cause at INFO); a store the write cannot replace refuses the call. Calls in flight whose snapshots were lost are told their check did not run, at ERROR, while the stamp is younger than FRESH_START_WINDOW_S.

A timed-out checklist is handed on, not passed: the file goes on the unchecked list, which is logged at WARNING (escalated by @trigger) and named in the block text. The gate fails OPEN by decision (gates.FAIL_OPEN): a stop it cannot finish must not trap the sub-agent.
Spelling only: with no project root the line names the test file by its absolute path instead of a project-relative one. The pointer still lands on the same file and no decision rests on it.
Display only: an unreadable start leaves the age out of the refusal text ("" or None both drop the "old" part). No decision rests on the age; ranking uses _session_start.
None is handed on as "cannot rank", never as "younger": _we_are_the_incumbent then answers False, so an unreadable start keeps the refusal of the newer seat. The refusal is the answer.

Fails closed: an unimportable admin_seat leaves the answer (None, False), so the caller is unnamed and never the admin seat, and every git refusal stands. The refusal is the answer; WARNING names the dark admin lane.
Fails closed: an unimportable admin_seat returns (None, False), so no seat is exempted and every delete refusal stands. The refusal is the answer; WARNING names the dark admin lane.

Fails toward the block: an errored file that cannot be read keeps every recorded error as found, so no error is dropped as a placeholder line. INFO, not WARNING: a just-deleted file is the usual cause, and the block it keeps is itself the signal.
None means "unknown", never clean: edit_gate keeps the recorded errors and the block stands when pyright is missing, times out or answers garbage. Each case logs at WARNING, which @trigger escalates.

One broken module costs its own verbs, never the whole drone @hooks menu: the loop skips it and the next module loads. It logs at ERROR, which @trigger escalates, and the missing verbs answer as unknown commands.

A ledger line without the turn number or automated flag is still a record; raising would lose the whole line. The field reads as null in the ledger and the WARNING, which @trigger escalates, names the broken cadence import.

Read-only: a corrupt inbox.json is never written here, it only drops the unread count from the compaction snapshot. Raising would lose the whole snapshot. WARNING, which @trigger escalates, names the read failure; @ai_mail owns the file.

The snapshot is still stamped, truncated at the default cap instead of the branch's own; raising here would lose the whole snapshot at compaction. WARNING, which @trigger escalates, names the dark @memory door.
Read-only: a corrupt local.json is never written here, it only drops the Last Session block from the post-compact injection. WARNING, which @trigger escalates, names the read failure.

The injection still runs when cadence cannot reset its counter; the cost is a regrounding cadence measured from before the compaction. Raising would lose the recovery block. WARNING, which @trigger escalates, names the failure.
The injection still runs when the grounding receipt cannot be set pending; the cost is one compaction the receipt verb does not track. It logs at ERROR, which @trigger escalates.
The re-ground still ships without its release-notice head; raising would lose the whole grounding for the sake of one notice. WARNING, which @trigger escalates, names the failure.

Only the log level of the DEGRADED line depends on the turn; an unreadable turn reads as None, which raises that line to WARNING. The kernel still goes out, so nothing the agent receives stands in for an answer.

The failure is handed on as text: cadence_down carries the exception into the kernel's banner, which tells the agent on every turn that the other loaders are WITHHELD and why. WARNING here, escalated by @trigger; the kernel fires alone by design (DPLAN-0347).

A dark window stamp costs only the per-window guard: the gauge guards per session instead, so after a compaction a nudge may stay quiet until the next session. The fill is still read and said. WARNING, which @trigger escalates, names the failure.
The guard file only stops the same context nudge repeating; if it cannot be written the agent sees the nudge again, which is itself the visible signal. No decision rests on it.
The context nudge still goes out without the receipt's line; the cost is one turn the grounding receipt does not record. It logs at ERROR, which @trigger escalates.

Read-only: alerts.json is @trigger's, written under its lock, and is never written here. An unreadable file shows no banner this prompt; WARNING, which @trigger escalates, names the read error, and drone @hooks dismiss prints it in red.
Fails toward showing: an alert whose expires_at cannot be read is kept active, so the banner is never hidden by a bad date; the agent can dismiss it by id.
The guard file only stops a banner being announced twice; if it cannot be written the agent sees the banner again, which is itself the visible signal. No decision rests on it.
Fails toward showing: a cadence that cannot answer lets the banner repeat every turn instead of hiding it. The WARNING says FAIL-OPEN and is escalated by @trigger.

A corrupt counter is never overwritten here (the parse fails before the write); it reads as turn 0, so the feedback line stays quiet for the session. Only a nag line is lost. WARNING, which @trigger escalates, names the failure.
Fails toward showing: a cadence that cannot answer announces any new mail instead of hiding it, so the agent still hears of it. WARNING, which @trigger escalates, names the broken cadence.
The stamp only spares a repeat check: if it cannot be written, the next compaction runs the rollover check again, which is the safe side. No decision is skipped on its account.

Append-only ledger, read and never rewritten from these rows: a torn line (two appends racing) costs that one row from the comment counts and the file is left as found. Raising would darken the whole comment budget for every later edit.

Boot-menu tmux lookups: no tmux, a garbled pane line or a failed ppid read only means the session's tmux host is not found, and _stop_session falls to SIGTERM by PID and says which it did on stderr. Nothing is skipped.
Display only: an unreadable start time, transcript mtime or lock timestamp drops the age from a boot-menu line. No choice or decision rests on the age.

Not a file read: a hook's stdout that opens with a brace but does not parse is judged as plain text, which is what Claude Code itself does with it, so the ledger records what really reached the model. No default stands in.

A write, not a read: a record that cannot be appended returns None and logs at WARNING "record NOT written (a gap in the ledger)", which @trigger escalates. Raising would break the dispatch the ledger only observes.
Append-only per-session ledger, read for the drone @hooks ledger view and never rewritten from these rows: a torn line costs that one row and the file is left as found.
Not a file read: a hook's stdout that opens with a brace but does not parse is plain text, exactly as Claude Code reads it, so the merge carries it as text. No default stands in for an answer.

Not a file read: None means "plain text", a legitimate engine answer the bridge carries as context. A deny never rests on the parse: exit 2 on a guarded event denies whatever the text, and the engine's stdin is parsed again by the engine itself.

Not a file read: None means "plain text", a legitimate engine answer the bridge carries as context. A deny never rests on the parse: exit 2 on a guarded event denies whatever the text, and the engine's stdin is parsed again by the engine itself.

Not a file read: None means "plain text", a legitimate engine answer the bridge carries as context. A deny never rests on the parse: exit 2 on a guarded event denies whatever the text, and the engine's stdin is parsed again by the engine itself.

A torn line in the provider's own transcript or rollout is skipped and the search goes on; an ack lost in it reads as not found, so the smoke turn FAILS rather than passes. The provider's file is only read, never written.

A restore, not a read: one branch file that cannot be put back is logged at ERROR (escalated by @trigger) with its path, and the loop still restores the rest. Raising would leave every later file unrestored.

A provider's stdout stream mixes JSON events with plain lines; a non-JSON line is skipped and the scan goes on. Nothing is defaulted: a session id or limit error never found reads as none, which the parity run reports as no data.

engine.jsonl and its rotated .1 are append-only and only read here: a generation that is absent or unreadable, or a torn line, costs those rows, and a session left with no rows is reported as NO_DATA, never as SAME.

An absent session pointer is a defined state (0.0 = never written); the run compares the stamp before and after, so a pointer that appears reads as moved. Only FileNotFoundError is caught: any other stat failure raises out of the run. Kept because the checker's absence pass needs a read call and stat is none.

Sound is cosmetic: a voice or chime that cannot play (piper timed out, no player) costs only that sound, and the hook's real output is already delivered. The event's engine.jsonl row still records the hook; a raise would only fail the hook for a missing beep.

resolve() fails only on a symlink loop or an unreadable cwd; the path as spelled still names the file, and the name lane judges that spelling. A protected name is refused either way, so nothing opens on it.

A cwd that cannot be resolved or scanned (deleted under the session, or unreadable) has no project or passport to read, so the seat reads as no manager and the notice is not built. Only an advisory notice is lost; no gate rests on it.
Read-only: a corrupt scaffold manifest is never written here; it only means no release notice is built. WARNING, which @trigger escalates, names the file; aipass init and aipass doctor own it.

HELD from a raise: an unreadable registry still marks the project boundary and branches are still told by the src/<pkg>/<branch> shape, but project-level files lose their fence. Raising would refuse every write in the project, the repair included. WARNING on each gated call, escalated by @trigger.
A host that publishes no PATH_MAX answers 0 and the length check falls to the real probe of the path, which still refuses an over-long one. Nothing is passed unjudged.

An edit's fragment is often not tokenizable on its own; the scan then counts the # lines directly, a second real measure, not a stand-in for an answer. Only docstring lines go uncounted, and only advisory comment budgets read the count.

Fails closed: None reads as no policy found, and load_policy turns that into the refusing Policy (_missing), so testwrite_gate refuses new test files. The refusal is the answer; its text names the search start.

An unreadable hooks.json narrows the crash pre-check to the engine's own root modules; it never widens what an edit may do. Raising would refuse every .py edit in the fleet.
